articles.headline: Contract Status and Ride Openings as the Off-Season Begins
articles.dek: Examining expiring deals and potential landing spots for top sim drivers.
articles.body:
With the 20th and final race of the season concluded at Kansas Speedway, attention shifts to the off-season market. Several prominent drivers enter the break with expiring contracts, creating notable intrigue in the garage. Alfie Denley, Caleb Guerrier, Nick Apollo, McCoy Behnke, Daniel Dominguez, and Tyler Payne all finish their current agreements at the conclusion of 2028.

Team adjustments are also taking shape further down the pit lane. Brady Hargrove remains signed through 2030 with Nitro Motorsports, though sources indicate friction regarding equipment performance after finishing thirty-second in points. Hot seat pressure also follows Kolby Newman, who struggled relative to his teammates and sits thirtieth in the standings, as well as Karson Mitchell after recording six DNFs.

In the truck ranks, McAnally-Hilgemann Racing faces potential movement with Christian Eckes potentially leaving his seat in the FedEx Freight entry. That opening could draw interest from top-tier sim racers looking to make a jump. Negotiations remain informal as teams finalize their crew chief pairings and sponsor commitments for the upcoming calendar year.

articles.headline: Reviewing the Numbers Behind the 2028 Season Field
articles.dek: A statistical look back at how the top names performed across twenty rounds of competition.
articles.body:
The 2028 season is officially in the books following the recent finale at Kansas Speedway. Tyler Payne secured the championship title with 3052 total points and two wins. His consistency proved vital over the twenty races, holding off Alfie Denley by 34 points in the final standings. Denley also collected two victories and finished the year with 3018 points.

William Faison led all drivers in the win column with four checkered flags, though he finished fifth in the final standings with 2801 points. Daniel Stavchanksy tallied three wins, ending his campaign eighth overall with 2687 points. McCoy Behnke, who won the season finale at Kansas after starting twenty-third and leading 71 laps, finished third in points with 2883 and two wins.

Moving through the standings, Nick Apollo claimed fourth with 2808 points and one win. Daniel Dominguez rounded out the top six at 2779 points with two wins, while Caleb Guerrier grabbed seventh with 2710 points and a single win. Vincent Crook took ninth with 2668 points and one win, and George Noble completed the top ten with 2658 points without visiting victory lane.

Mid-pack battles defined much of the year, with Brenden Gregg finishing eleventh on 2628 points. Evan Pruitt captured one win and ended the year twelfth with 2474 points. Ryan Davis, Aaron Kyan, Parker Pettigrew, and Parker Teague rounded out the remaining full-time contenders in the points order. The off-season is now underway across the garage.

articles.headline: Behnke Charges from Deep to Win Menards 150 at Kansas
articles.dek: McCoy Behnke drove from twenty-third on the grid to capture his second win of the sim-racing season in the finale at Kansas Speedway.
articles.body:
McCoy Behnke drove a brilliant race through the field at Kansas Speedway, working his way from the twenty-third starting spot to win the Menards 150 by 0.402 seconds. The victory capped off the twentieth and final round of the simulated ARCA Menards Series season, closing out a grueling intermediate track battle marked by nine caution periods.

Alfie Denley pushed Behnke to the finish line, securing second place after leading 28 laps from his sixth starting position. Brenden Gregg put together a strong run from nineteenth on the grid to finish third, adding 27 laps led to his afternoon. Daniel Stavchanksy and Atsz Minyoung rounded out the top five, with Stavchanksy climbing from fourteenth to fourth while pacing the field for 23 circuits.

The race required heavy tire management and careful navigation of a frequent yellow flag rhythm. Thirty-two cars took the green flag, but attrition took a toll as the long-run speed separated the contenders. Sekani Hildebrand earned the biggest mover honors of the afternoon, slicing through traffic from thirty-second on the starting grid to finish seventh.

When the checkered flag dropped, Tyler Payne cemented his grasp on the sim league championship with 3052 total points and two wins. Alfie Denley finished the standings in the runner-up spot with 3018 points, followed by McCoy Behnke in third at 2883 points. Nick Apollo and William Faison closed out the top five in the final championship tally.

Teams now head into a well-earned offseason to evaluate setups, driver lineups, and mechanical packages for the next simulated campaign.

articles.headline: The ARCA Menards Series silly season: who is going where in 2028
articles.dek: The offseason shuffling is complete as the garage prepares to drop the green flag on the 2028 campaign.
articles.body:
The garage doors are up and the preseason noise is finally settling across the ARCA Menards Series pit lane. While the points race has yet to officially kick off, the offseason departures have left massive shoes to fill for some of the series' heavy-hitting organizations.

Front Row Motorsports and Tricon Garage came calling during the winter months, poaching top tier talent straight out of the ARCA ranks. Valdemar Estriden packed his bags after leaving Pinnacle Racing Group, securing a massive promotion to the Craftsman Truck Series with Front Row Motorsports in the number 34 machine.

Not to be outdone, Samuel Riggs also made the jump to the Truck Series. Riggs vacated his ride at Nitro Motorsports to take over the wheel of the number 17 entry for Tricon Garage, leaving a pair of prime vacancies in the process.

Nitro Motorsports wasted no time filling those empty seats with fresh blood for the upcoming year. Twenty-one-year-old rookie Brady Hargrove steps into the number 15 machine, while seventeen-year-old Parker Teague takes over the number 25 entry.

These new pairings will define the early weeks of the schedule as the rookies get up to speed against the series veterans. With the grid nearly set, teams are finalizing their final paint schemes and crew chief pairings before everyone unloads for the season opener.

chase.headline: The Regular Season Ledger is Closed
chase.summary: With all 20 rounds officially in the books, Tyler Payne secures the simulated crown with 3052 points and a 100 percent statistical projection. Alfie Denley follows closely behind at 3018 points to lock down second in the final standings. Every single projected qualifier cleared the bar cleanly in this 2500-run simulation model.

notes.tyler payne: Tyler Payne finishes at the summit with 3052 points, holding off the entire field.
notes.alfie denley: Alfie Denley claims second with 3018 points after a stellar campaign.
notes.mccoy behnke: McCoy Behnke rounds out the podium positions with 2883 points.

race.headline: Wrapping Up the Year in Style
race.summary: McCoy Behnke stole the final headlines by charging from twenty-third to take the checkered flag. Meanwhile, Aaron Kyan muscled his way from thirteenth to third while pacing 36 laps, and Vincent Crook sliced through traffic from twelfth to finish right behind the winner.

notes.mccoy behnke: McCoy Behnke drove all the way from twenty-third to park it in victory lane.
notes.aaron kyan: Aaron Kyan put on a show by marching from P13 to P3 and leading 36 circuits.
notes.vincent crook: Vincent Crook climbed ten spots from twelfth to secure second place at the finish.

season.headline: Reflecting on Twenty Rounds of Hard Racing
season.summary: Tyler Payne proved unstoppable over the full schedule, converting short track prowess into a commanding title run. Alfie Denley kept him honest all year long, finishing just thirty-four points back in the final tally. Further down the order, drivers like Evan Pruitt locked up twelfth with 2474 points to cap off the top tier.

notes.tyler payne: Tyler Payne stands alone at the top with 3052 points to claim the title.
notes.alfie denley: Alfie Denley secured second with 3018 points through consistent speed.
notes.evan pruitt: Evan Pruitt wraps up his campaign in twelfth position with 2474 points.
